question.text: A resistor develops <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>300</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi></math> of thermal energy in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>15</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>, when a current of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> is passed through it. If the current increases to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math>, the energy developed in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi></math>.

solution.text:
Energy produced is given by H=i2Rt

When i=2 A, t=15 s, energy is H=300=22×R×15

Resistance is R=5 Ω

When i=3 A, t=10 s.

Energy is H'=32×5×10=450 J
